title: What Is a Cleaning-Chemical Concentrate?
excerpt: A cleaning-chemical concentrate is a product supplied at a higher ingredient concentration than its intended use solution and designed to be prepared only according to its label or approved dispensing system.
content_html:
A cleaning-chemical concentrate is a product supplied in a more concentrated form than the solution intended for routine use. Concentrates are designed to be converted into a use solution through a controlled manufacturer-specified process, often using a dispensing system.

Why concentrates exist

Concentrated formats can reduce packaging, storage volume and transport of water. They can also support consistent use when paired with a correctly configured dispensing system.

A concentrate is not automatically ready to use

The fact that a product is liquid does not mean it is intended to be applied directly. The label or technical instructions define whether it is a concentrate, a ready-to-use product or another format.

The label defines the intended use solution

CDC guidance says environmental cleaning products should be prepared according to manufacturer instructions because both under-concentration and over-concentration can reduce effectiveness or create unnecessary risk.

Dispensing systems help control consistency

Where facilities use automatic dispensing, the system should be maintained and calibrated according to the approved program. The goal is repeatability rather than estimation by colour, smell or foam.

Concentrates can require additional controls

Because concentrates contain more product per unit volume, labels and safety data may specify handling, storage or protective measures. Those requirements should be followed by trained staff.

Practical takeaway

A concentrate is a supply format, not a cue to guess how much product to use. The manufacturer label and approved dispensing process determine the intended use solution.

References

  1. CDC — Cleaning Supplies and Equipment.
  2. US EPA — Safer Choice Standard and Criteria.
